land.text: Baekje's last Cliopatria outline (656..660): 'created in place of Baekje in present-day Chungcheong Province after its defeat by a joint Silla-Tang alliance'

predecessors.note: 'In 660, the coalition troops of Silla and Tang China attacked Paekche, resulting in the annexation of Paekche by Silla.' The monk Dochim and the former general Buyeo Boksin 'rose to restore the kingdom'.

land.text: Juryu (Churyu), the restoration's headquarters 'in modern Seocheon County': by 662 the 'area of control was confined to the fortress of Churyu and its immediate vicinity'

successors.note: The Silla-Tang forces 'won a decisive victory' at Baekgang; Juryu fell to them (undated on the page).

capitals.name: Juryu (Churyu) castle, Seocheon
capitals.note: 'Juryu was the restoration's headquarters', 'in modern Seocheon County'. The coordinate is Seocheon town (not in the gazetteer).

correction.text: the Baekje heartland the movement rose in; the Battle page gives no extent for 660-661

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page gives no territory before 662 ('By 662 the area of control was confined to the fortress of Churyu and its immediate vicinity'), so the earlier extent is a placeholder (confidence 1). The Ungjin page says the movement 'based at Juryu castle'.

correction.text: Juryu (Churyu), the restoration's headquarters 'in modern Seocheon County': by 662 the 'area of control was confined to the fortress of Churyu and its immediate vicinity'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the area of control 'confined to the fortress of Churyu and its immediate vicinity' by 662 (Battle of Baekgang page). The 30 km radius round Seocheon stands for the fortress and its vicinity.

region.text: the Baekje heartland: Dochim and Buyeo Boksin 'rose to restore the kingdom' after the 660 fall of Baekje

ledger.note: 660: Baekje loyalists rise against the Tang-Silla occupation. 'The monk Dochim and former general Buyeo Boksin rose to restore the kingdom' and 'welcomed the Paekche prince Buyeo Pung back from Japan to serve as king'; the page dates neither the rising nor Pung's return. The year follows the 660 conquest (confidence 1); Ungjin (the Tang occupation) is the counterpart.

minus.text: Juryu (Churyu), the restoration's headquarters 'in modern Seocheon County': by 662 the 'area of control was confined to the fortress of Churyu and its immediate vicinity'

region.text: the restoration's land beyond Juryu, lost by 662

ledger.note: 662: the movement is reduced to Juryu. 'By 662, the restoration's area of control was confined to the fortress of Churyu and its immediate vicinity.' The page does not say who took the rest; the Tang-Silla occupation is assumed.

region.text: Juryu (Churyu), the restoration's headquarters 'in modern Seocheon County': by 662 the 'area of control was confined to the fortress of Churyu and its immediate vicinity'

ledger.note: October 663: Juryu falls and the movement is crushed. The Silla-Tang forces 'won a decisive victory, compelling Yamato Japan to withdraw ... and crushing the Paekche restoration movement' at Baekgang on 27-28 August 663 (lunar; 4-5 October Julian). The page gives no date for Juryu's fall or for Boksin's death (killed by Pung 'for fear of insurrection').

region.text: Juryu (Churyu), the restoration's headquarters 'in modern Seocheon County': by 662 the 'area of control was confined to the fortress of Churyu and its immediate vicinity'

ledger.note: October 663: the restored Baekje ends. 'Paekche falls and is absorbed by the alliance' (infobox).

notes: Rebel dossier for the Baekje loyalists (660-663). No Wikipedia article for the movement was found under the titles tried (Baekje revival movement did not load). Dates: the pages give no year for the rising, for Pung's return from Japan (661 or 662 elsewhere) or for the fall of Juryu; 663 and October (Julian) come from the battle date. The Seocheon coordinate used for the capital is the town's, approximate. Compare the baekje dossier (jk-02-b), which has this as a war only.
